summary: Describes the extensions to CR-LDP signaling needed to support Generalized MPLS, which broadens the MPLS control plane to time-division, wavelength and spatial switching, such as in SONET, SDH and optical networks.

eli5.summary: This is the version of the GMPLS rules written for one signaling system, CR-LDP, so it can set up paths in optical and similar networks.

subtitle: The CR-LDP version of GMPLS signaling for time-division, wavelength and fiber switched networks.

tldr.problem: MPLS signaling was built for packet interfaces, but Generalized MPLS needs to set up paths over time-division (SONET/SDH), wavelength (optical lambda) and fiber or port switching as well.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3472 defines the new CR-LDP TLVs and procedures for this, including a Generalized Label Request, Generalized Label, Label Set, Upstream Label for bidirectional LSPs, Admin Status, protection and interface identification.
tldr.outcome: It is the CR-LDP counterpart to the RSVP-TE version in RFC 3473, and it has since been updated by RFC 3468 and RFC 4201.

facts.label: Label Set actions
facts.value: 0 and 1 add or exclude labels; 2 and 3 add or exclude ranges

today: RFC 3472 is a Proposed Standard that has been updated by RFC 3468 and RFC 4201. The RSVP-TE version of the same extensions is RFC 3473.

sections.title: GMPLS Signaling over CR-LDP
sections.content:
Generalized MPLS extends MPLS from packet (PSC) interfaces and switching to three more classes: Time-Division Multiplex (TDM), Lambda Switch (LSC) and Fiber-Switch (FSC). The functional description of the signaling extensions is in RFC 3471, which this document parallels. RFC 3472 supplies the CR-LDP specific formats and mechanisms for all four classes, and the RSVP-TE version is in RFC 3473.

One difference is called out. RSVP-TE has a rapid failure notification mechanism, but CR-LDP does not. When a failure is detected it propagates outward from the point of failure with RELEASE and WITHDRAW messages, resources are released, and actual resource information may be fed back to the source.
sections.eli5: There are two booking systems for these tracks. This RFC is the instruction sheet for one of them. The other has its own sheet.

sections.title: Label Related TLVs
sections.content:
Section 2 defines the label-related Type, Length, Value (TLV) formats carried in CR-LDP messages.

  • The Generalized Label Request (type 0x0824) is set by the ingress node in a REQUEST message, passed transparently by transit nodes and used by the egress. It carries an LSP Encoding Type, a Switching Type and a G-PID. The Switching Type may be updated hop by hop.
  • The Generalized Label (0x0825) travels upstream in MAPPING messages. A MAPPING message with both a generalized and a normal label is a protocol error.
  • The Waveband Label (0x0828) uses the generalized label format with a Waveband Id, a Start Label and an End Label. If wavelengths are mirrored when one waveband is switched to another, the start and end labels MUST be swapped before forwarding, in both directions for a bidirectional tunnel.
  • The Suggested Label (type 0x904) has the generalized label format and is used in REQUEST messages. Errors in received suggested labels MUST be ignored.
  • The Label Set (0x0827) restricts the labels that may be used downstream. It has an Action field: 0 and 1 add or exclude specific labels, and 2 and 3 add or exclude ranges.

Nodes check each requested parameter against the incoming interface, the node and the outgoing interface. When a check fails they MUST send a NOTIFICATION message with a "Routing problem" indication, for example Unsupported Encoding, Switching Type, Unsupported G-PID or Label Set. Bandwidth is carried in the Peak and Committed Data Rate fields of the CR-LDP Traffic Parameters TLV.
sections.eli5: The request says what kind of connection you want, and the answer says exactly which slot you got. You can also say "only these slots, please" to avoid being given one that will not work.

sections.title: Bidirectional LSPs and Label Errors
sections.content:
A bidirectional LSP is signaled by putting an Upstream Label (type 0x0826, same format as the generalized label) in the REQUEST message. It MUST indicate a label that is valid for forwarding at the time the request is sent. The receiver checks it and, if unacceptable, MUST send a NOTIFICATION with "Routing problem/Unacceptable label value". An intermediate node must allocate a label on its outgoing interface and set up internal data paths before it fills in an outgoing Upstream Label. The terminator can use the upstream label at once to send data back towards the initiator. When the LSP is removed, both labels become invalid.

To help recovery from label errors, a NOTIFICATION message may carry an Acceptable Label Set TLV (type 0x082a). It has the same format and add or exclude procedures as the Label Set. Including it is optional, and its absence has no specific meaning.
sections.eli5: For a two-way road you must pick a lane for each direction before you start. If the lane you picked is blocked, the answer can say which lanes would have been fine.

sections.title: Explicit Labels and Protection
sections.content:
The Label ER-Hop TLV (type 0x0829) gives explicit control over the label used on a link. It follows an ER-Hop holding the IP address or interface identifier of the link. Up to two may be present, one for the downstream label and one for the upstream label (U-bit set). A node copies a downstream value into a new Label Set TLV, or an acceptable upstream value into a new Upstream Label TLV, in the outgoing REQUEST, then removes the label ER-Hops. Bad arrangements, such as a U-bit label ER-Hop on a unidirectional LSP, SHOULD result in "Bad EXPLICIT_ROUTE" errors.

The optional Protection TLV (type 0x0835) indicates protection attributes of an LSP. Transit nodes MUST check that the outgoing interface or tunnel can satisfy the requested protection. If not they MUST send a NOTIFICATION with "Routing problem/Unsupported Link Protection".
sections.eli5: Sometimes the person booking wants to say exactly which track to use at one stop. Another option is to ask for a spare track in case the first one breaks.

sections.title: Administrative Status and Deletion
sections.content:
The optional Admin Status TLV (type 0x082b) carries the administrative state of an LSP. It holds a Reflect (R) bit and T, A and D bits. It can ride in REQUEST and MAPPING messages, or in a NOTIFICATION to ask for a change of state. Transit nodes update local state and propagate it. If an egress node receives it with R set, it SHOULD reflect the same values, except R, in a MAPPING message.

In optical networks it is useful to set the administrative status before tearing an LSP down. From the ingress, the ingress sends a NOTIFICATION with the R and D bits set, and the egress SHOULD then respond with a LABEL WITHDRAW. From the egress, the egress sends a NOTIFICATION with D set, and the ingress sends a LABEL RELEASE downstream. A node that sends a notification with D set MUST verify that it receives a LABEL RELEASE within a configurable time, 30 seconds by default (SHOULD). Otherwise it SHOULD send a release downstream and a withdraw upstream.
sections.eli5: Before closing a shop you hang up a "closing soon" sign so everyone can get ready. If nobody confirms within a short time, you close it anyway.

sections.title: Control Channel Separation and Faults
sections.content:
In optical networks the control channel may not travel with the data channel. For these links the sender of the REQUEST picks the data interface and names it with an Interface ID (IF_ID) TLV (IPv4 type 0x082d, IPv6 type 0x082e). For a unidirectional LSP a downstream data channel MUST be indicated. For a bidirectional LSP over a bundled link, the upstream data channel can differ from the downstream one. The receiver saves the values and returns them in the MAPPING message. A node that finds the TLV inconsistent with a received ERO MUST send a LABEL ABORT with "Bad Explicit Routing TLV Error".

To tie an error to a specific interface, a node SHOULD put an IF_ID Status TLV (IPv4 0x082f, IPv6 0x0830) in the LABEL WITHDRAW or LABEL RELEASE message.

On fault handling, failures in the signaling channel should not affect existing optical connections, and a recovery procedure SHALL guarantee connection integrity at both ends. The RFC refers to the LDP fault tolerance draft for the recovery procedures.
sections.eli5: Sometimes the phone line that sets up a call is separate from the line the call travels on. So the message must say which line carries the call, and a broken phone line must not cut calls that are already going.

sections.title: Security and IANA Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC states that it introduces no new security considerations to RFC 3212, the base CR-LDP specification.

It uses the LDP (RFC 3036) name spaces and lists fourteen TLV assignments: Generalized Label Request 0x0824, Generalized Label 0x0825, Upstream Label 0x0826, Label Set 0x0827, Waveband Label 0x0828, ER-Hop 0x0829, Acceptable Label Set 0x082a, Admin Status 0x082b, Interface ID 0x082c, IPv4 Interface ID 0x082d, IPv6 Interface ID 0x082e, IPv4 IF_ID Status 0x082f, IPv6 IF_ID Status 0x0830 and Protection 0x0835.
sections.eli5: Each new kind of note gets its own number in the official list, so nobody mixes them up. Nothing here makes things less safe than before.

fields.name: U
fields.desc: Flag bit at the start of every CR-LDP TLV.

fields.desc: Second flag bit of the TLV.

fields.desc: Encoding of the LSP; as specific as possible.

fields.name: Switching Type
fields.desc: Switching type; may be updated hop by hop.

fields.name: G-PID
fields.desc: Normally examined only at the egress.
